history.title: History
history.sub: Every dictation is saved before it is typed, so nothing is lost if the text lands in the wrong window.
history.empty_sub: Press your shortcut and they will show up here.
settings.title: Settings
settings.sub: Applied to the daemon without restarting it.
settings.shortcut_help: Click Change, then press the combination you want. The final key is swallowed by localflow, so ctrl+win will not open the Start menu.
settings.hold_help: Hold the key while you speak
settings.toggle_help: One press starts, one press stops. Hands free.
settings.max_dictation_help: Safety net if the microphone stays open.
settings.language_help: The language you dictate in. It drives the model and the word analysis on Your voice — it is not the language of this window.
settings.corrections_help: Proper nouns that keep coming out wrong. Matching ignores case.
settings.overlay_help: A small marker on screen while listening.
settings.startup_help: The model loads once, when the session opens.
settings.ui_language_help: The language of this window. Independent from the language you dictate in.
usage.title: Stats
usage.sub: Everything is computed on this machine, from your history. Nothing is sent anywhere.
usage.where_help: The target application has only been recorded since the 1 August update: earlier dictations are not counted here.
voice.title: Your voice
voice.sub: A portrait obtained by counting, not by a language model: every statement traces back to a number measured on your dictations.
voice.empty: Not enough text yet to draw a portrait.
voice.empty_sub: Dictate for a few minutes, then come back.
voice.catchphrase_none: No phrase comes back often enough yet.
status.title: Status
status.sub: What the daemon is doing right now.
status.restarted: Daemon restarted, the model is reloading…
status.duplicates: {n} other instance(s) of the service are running. Restarting will leave only one.
about.title: About
about.p1: localflow turns speech into text, locally, with no account and no quota. The shortcut writes into the focused field of any application.
about.p2: Transcription happens while you speak: the sentence is cut on silences and each chunk is sent off as it comes. When you release, only the tail is left to process — hence a latency of about a tenth of a second whatever the length dictated.
about.p3: The model is parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3, running on the CPU through ONNX. Nothing leaves the machine: no audio, no text, no network request.
